## Services
- [Hardwood Flooring](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/hardwood-flooring/): Wide-plank European white oak, engineered American oak, solid hickory and walnut — installed by hand, acclimated for the Gulf Coast, and warranted for two years in writing.
- [Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) Flooring](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/vinyl-plank-flooring/): Fully waterproof. Scratch-resistant. Dimensionally stable in Florida humidity. The smartest dollar-per-square-foot floor you can put in a Sarasota kitchen, family room, or short-term rental.
- [Tile Installation](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/tile-installation/): Porcelain, ceramic, natural stone, and large-format slab — set flat, set straight, set to the slope your shower pan actually needs. TCNA-spec substrate prep on every install.
- [Laminate Flooring](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/laminate-flooring/): AC4 and AC5 commercial-grade laminate — the highest scratch resistance of any wood-look flooring at a fraction of hardwood pricing. Right answer for kids, pets, and rental properties.
- [Stair Treads](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/stair-treads/): Engineered hardwood, solid oak, LVP, and laminate stair treads — fitted to your existing stringers, matched to your field floor, and finished in your home in two days.
- [Floor Repair](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/floor-repair/): Cupped hardwood. Cracked tile. Lifting LVP seams. Squeaky subfloors. Stair-tread loosening. We diagnose, scope, and repair — no full floor replacement when a targeted fix will do.

## Flooring answers
- [What's the Best Flooring Option for a House by the Water?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/whats-best-flooring-option-house-by-water/): For a home directly on the water in Sarasota or Manatee County, porcelain tile is the flooring pros reach for most often: it resists the 0.5% water-absorption test that defines porcelain, and it shrugs off sand, wet guests and open-window humidity that wear down wood. Below the base flood elevation, FEMA's guidance only allows its top two damage-resistance classes, so ask your flood consultant before installing anything else there.
- [Which Is Better in Florida Humidity, Waterproof Laminate or LVP?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/waterproof-laminate-vs-luxury-vinyl-plank-better-florida/): Waterproof laminate and luxury vinyl plank cost about the same — This Old House puts laminate installed at $5-$12/sq ft and vinyl plank at $5-$20/sq ft. Their warranties differ more: Pergo's WetProtect laminate covers spills and pet accidents but excludes flooding and standing water. Our verdict: LVP is the safer pick near Sarasota-area kitchens, bathrooms and lanais; laminate works fine in drier living spaces.
- [Can Water-Damaged Hardwood Floors Be Saved?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/water-damaged-hardwood-floors-saved/): Often, yes, if the moisture source gets fixed first and nobody sands the boards too early. Mild cupping can flatten on its own over several weeks to months once moisture-meter readings return to normal; sanding before that point tends to cause crowning instead. Angi's 2026 data puts average hardwood floor repair cost at $1,078 nationally, with a typical range of $482 to $1,707.
- [Can Vinyl Plank Flooring Be Saved After a Flood?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/vinyl-plank-flooring-saved-after-flood/): Sometimes, if the water was clean and you act fast. Click-together vinyl plank can often be lifted, cleaned, dried and relaid, but the pad or cork underlayment beneath it should be discarded and the slab dried and retested before reinstalling. Water contaminated by storm surge or sewage, common after a Sarasota-area hurricane, usually means the flooring needs to be replaced rather than salvaged.
- [Is Vinyl Plank Flooring Actually Waterproof?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/vinyl-plank-flooring-really-waterproof/): Yes at the surface, but not automatically underneath: in a Sarasota-area home on a slab, most floating LVP/LVT makers still cap allowable moisture at 75-85% relative humidity, so a waterproof plank doesn't remove the need for a dry slab. After a clean-water event, planks can often be lifted, dried and re-laid within the EPA's 24-48 hour mold-prevention window.
- [Why Does Vinyl Plank Flooring Buckle or Peak?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/vinyl-plank-floor-buckling/): In Sarasota-area homes, vinyl plank floors usually buckle because they have nowhere to expand: COREtec's install guide calls for a 1/4-inch gap at every wall, and planks pinned tight by trim, door jambs or a glued transition strip peak first, especially in sun-heated rooms. An uneven slab makes it worse — Shaw's SPC guide requires the concrete to be flat within 3/16 inch over 10 feet before installation.
- [Can You Use a Steam Mop on Vinyl Plank or Hardwood Floors?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/use-steam-mop-vinyl-plank-hardwood-floors/): No, not on vinyl plank or hardwood. Shaw's resilient flooring care guide says plainly not to use steam cleaners on resilient flooring, and Angi warns steam can warp planks and break down the seam adhesive. Hardwood faces the same risk from heat and trapped moisture. Steam damage isn't covered under a manufacturer's warranty or our 2-year workmanship warranty, so a damp microfiber mop is the safer routine for Sarasota-area homes.
- [How Many Sandings Does Your Floor Have Left In It?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/times-refinish-hardwood-engineered-floors/): In a Sarasota-area home, solid 3/4 in. hardwood can typically be refinished about 4 times over its life, sometimes up to 10 light screen-and-recoats. Engineered hardwood is more limited: a 2mm wear layer supports 1-2 sandings, 3mm supports 2-3, and 4mm supports 3-4, since each full sanding removes roughly 0.5mm to 1mm of wood.
- [What Wear Layer Thickness Do You Actually Need?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/thick-wear-layer-engineered-hardwood/): Engineered hardwood wear layers typically run 2mm to 4mm thick. A 2mm layer supports one or two sandings, 3mm supports two or three, and 4mm supports three or four - each full sanding removes roughly 0.5mm to 1mm of wood. If you want your floor refinished more than once, ask for at least a 3mm wear layer before you buy.
- [How Do You Test a Concrete Slab for Moisture Before Installing Flooring?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/test-concrete-slab-moisture-before-installing-flooring/): Concrete slabs get tested with ASTM F2170 relative humidity probes, set at 40% of slab depth, or ASTM F1869 calcium chloride tests measuring vapor emission over 24 hours. The default acceptable reading is 75% RH or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours, unless the flooring manufacturer specifies a higher limit, and we run this before quoting any wood or vinyl job on a Sarasota-area slab.
- [Does Direct Sunlight Damage Vinyl Plank Floors?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/sunlight-damage-vinyl-plank-flooring/): Yes. Both COREtec and Shaw's care guides warn against prolonged direct sunlight on vinyl plank, since heat buildup can discolor the wear layer and cause thermal expansion at sliding doors. Sarasota-area rooms with unshaded west-facing glass are most at risk. UV-blocking window film runs roughly $200-$500 per window, a common fix homeowners pair with drapes or blinds during peak sun hours.
- [Which Vinyl Plank Core Handles Florida Heat Better, SPC or WPC?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/spc-vs-wpc-vinyl-plank-core-better-florida/): SPC (stone-plastic composite) tolerates Florida heat better than WPC (wood-plastic composite): COREtec rates its SPC lines for -25°F to 155°F after installation, versus just 32°F to 100°F for WPC lines, and only floating installs are approved for three-season rooms with no climate control. Our verdict: pick SPC for a lanai, Florida room, or garage-adjacent space; WPC suits air-conditioned living areas.
- [How Soon Do I Have to Pull Up Wet Flooring After Storm Surge?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/soon-pull-up-wet-flooring-after-storm-surge/): Within 24 to 48 hours, per EPA guidance on water-damaged materials, is the window before mold risk climbs sharply. After storm surge specifically, that clock starts as soon as it's safe to re-enter the home, not once power or contractors are available. Helene's 2024 surge alone damaged an estimated 7,600 residences in unincorporated Sarasota County, which is why fast removal matters across an entire neighborhood, not just one house.
- [Solid or Engineered Hardwood: Which One Handles a Slab?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/solid-vs-engineered-hardwood-better-concrete-slab/): Engineered hardwood is the better choice on a concrete slab in Sarasota and Manatee counties. NWFA guidance says solid wood shouldn't go below grade, and most local homes are slab-on-grade. Engineered hardwood over a slab that tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) runs about $9-$20 per sq ft installed in 2026.
- [What Should I Set My AC and Humidistat to When I Leave My Florida Home for the Summer?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/set-ac-humidistat-leave-florida-home-summer-floors/): Leave the AC running at 85°F or lower, per UF/IFAS guidance for closing a seasonal home, since higher settings let indoor humidity pass 55-60% and put wood floors at risk. Southwest Florida HVAC companies recommend a tighter 78-80°F thermostat with the humidistat near 55-60%, calibrated before you leave for the summer.
- [Is It Worth Replacing Your Floors Before You List Your House?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/replace-floors-before-selling-house/): It depends on your floor's condition, not a blanket rule. If flooring is worn, stained or visibly dated, replacing it before listing usually pays for itself; the 2022 NAR/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found new wood flooring recovered 118% of its cost at resale. If your existing floor is in decent shape, a refinish or targeted repair is often the better return for less money and less time before closing.
- [Can I Replace My Florida Condo's Carpet With Tile or Hardwood?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/replace-carpet-florida-condo-tile-hardwood/): Yes, in most Florida condos you can swap carpet for tile or hardwood, but Florida Statute 718.113 lets your association's declaration control the swap, not the statute itself. Expect to submit an application, meet your building's IIC/STC minimum, 50 at a minimum under Florida's building code, and install an approved acoustic underlayment before the floor goes down.
- [Can You Have Real Hardwood Floors in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/real-hardwood-floors-florida/): Yes -- solid hardwood can work in a Sarasota or Manatee County home, but only above grade with air conditioning holding steady. NWFA guidelines put hardwood's comfort zone at 30-50% relative humidity and 60-80°F, and any concrete slab must test at or below 75% RH (ASTM F2170) before engineered hardwood glues down directly.
- [What Should You Ask a Flooring Contractor Before You Hire One?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/questions-ask-flooring-contractor-before-hiring/): Before hiring a flooring contractor in Sarasota or Manatee County, ask for a written itemized quote covering material, labor, removal and prep, proof of general liability insurance and workers' compensation, and how they test slab moisture. ASTM F2170 caps in-slab relative humidity at 75% before flooring goes down unless the manufacturer allows a higher reading.
- [Does Vinyl Plank Work on a Staircase?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/put-vinyl-plank-flooring-stairs/): Vinyl plank can go on stairs, but it must be fully glued down, not floated, and most LVP lines don't include a matching stair-nose profile that meets Florida's 3/4 in. to 1-1/4 in. nosing code. Many Sarasota-area homeowners end up with hardwood or engineered treads stained to match instead, since glued-on vinyl nosings tend to work loose within a year or two.
- [Can You Put Vinyl Plank Flooring on a Lanai or Florida Room With No AC?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/put-vinyl-plank-flooring-lanai-florida-room-no/): In a Sarasota-area lanai or Florida room with no AC, yes — if you choose the right core and float it rather than glue it: COREtec approves those spaces only for floating installs, rating SPC for -25°F to 155°F versus just 32°F to 100°F for WPC. Direct sun still matters separately, so an unshaded lanai needs film or blinds even with the right core.
- [What Does Porcelain Tile Installation Cost Per Square Foot?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/porcelain-tile-installation-cost-per-square-foot/): Installed porcelain or ceramic tile typically runs $6 to $15 per square foot in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026. Standard 12-18 in. tile costs $6-$10, large-format 24 in.-plus tile costs $9-$15, and wood-look plank tile costs $8-$13. Large-format tile costs more because it demands a flatter substrate and more precise layout to avoid lippage.
- [Is a Permit Required to Replace Flooring in Sarasota County?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/permit-replace-flooring-sarasota-county/): Sarasota County generally treats flooring replacement, tile, vinyl plank, hardwood or laminate, as cosmetic work that doesn't require a building permit, as long as there's no change to the subfloor structure or layout. Condo buildings are the exception: HOA rules on sound underlayment can still apply even when the county doesn't require a permit. Confirm specifics with the county building department for your address.
- [Does Changing Your Condo's Flooring Need a Permit in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/permit-change-flooring-florida-condo/): It depends on your city and your association. Several Florida cities, including Miami, Miami Beach, Boca Raton and Tampa, require a building permit plus an acoustic affidavit for hard-surface flooring in condos. Regardless of local permit rules, the Florida Building Code requires floor-ceiling assemblies between dwelling units to meet IIC and STC ratings of 50, or 45 if field-tested, which is what most HOA flooring rules are built around.
- [Does Replacing Your Flooring Actually Add Home Value?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/new-flooring-increase-home-value/): Yes, and refinishing pays back more than replacing. The 2022 National Association of Realtors/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found hardwood floor refinishing recovered 147% of its cost at resale, while installing new wood flooring recovered 118%. A typical $3,400 refinish added about $5,000 in perceived value, according to the same report.
- [Can Mold Grow Under Vinyl Plank Flooring on a Florida Slab?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/mold-grow-under-vinyl-plank-flooring-florida-slab/): Yes -- mold can grow under vinyl plank on a Florida slab when the concrete emits moisture above the flooring's rated limit, commonly 75% to 85% relative humidity. Floating installation doesn't remove this risk, it just changes how the failure shows up. The EPA says materials should dry within 24-48 hours after any water event to keep mold from establishing.
- [Do I Need a Moisture Barrier Under Vinyl Plank on a Concrete Slab?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/moisture-barrier-under-vinyl-plank-flooring-concrete-slab/): It depends on the product, but often yes. Most floating LVP and LVT makers cap acceptable in-slab relative humidity at 75% to 85%; some rigid SPC lines allow up to 90% RH or 8 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours within the manufacturer's tested system. A slab above the rated limit needs a vapor-retarder layer before vinyl plank goes down in a Sarasota-area home.
- [Do You Need a Moisture Barrier Under Laminate on a Concrete Floor?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/moisture-barrier-under-laminate-concrete-floor/): Yes, in a Sarasota-area home on a slab. Mohawk's laminate installation guide requires a moisture barrier over any concrete floor — 6-mil polyethylene film with seams overlapped 8 inches for a floating install. The slab should also test within ASTM F1869's default limit of 3 lbs of moisture vapor emission per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours, unless the manufacturer allows a higher reading.
- [LVP or Porcelain Tile: Which Is Better for a Florida House?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/lvp-vs-porcelain-tile-better-florida-house/): For most Sarasota-area homes, LVP installs faster and costs less than porcelain tile — a two-person crew can lay about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in 1-2 days on a flat, prepped slab, while tile takes longer because of cure times. Our verdict: choose LVP for speed and warmth underfoot, porcelain for wet areas and long-term durability.
- [Is LVP or Tile the Smarter Pick for a Long-Term Rental?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/lvp-tile-smarter-choice-long-term-rental-property/): For a long-term Florida rental, 20-mil rigid-core LVP typically installs for $2.75-$5.50 per square foot versus roughly $6-$10 for 12-18 inch porcelain tile, per local 2026 ranges. LVP is cheaper and faster to replace between tenants; tile lasts longer under heavy traffic but costs more up front and takes longer to redo.
- [How Long Does It Take to Replace the Floors in a Whole House?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/long-take-replace-floors-whole-house/): A two-person crew lays about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days on a flat, prepped slab. Tile and glue-down wood take longer because of cure times: tile needs 24 hours before grouting and up to 72 hours before heavy loads, and a full hardwood sand-and-refinish runs three to five working days.
- [How Many Days Should You Budget for Refinishing?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/long-take-refinish-hardwood-floors/): A full hardwood floor sand-and-refinish takes 3-5 working days from the first sanding pass to the last coat. Oil-based polyurethane needs up to 30 days to fully cure before furniture and rugs go back down, and Sarasota's summer humidity can stretch that further, so we build extra dry time into jobs scheduled June through September.
- [How Long Does a Slab Need to Dry After Flooding Before New Floors Go In?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/long-slab-dry-after-flooding-before-new-floors/): There's no universal number of days, despite what general guides claim. A flooded slab is ready when it tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours (ASTM F1869), the same default limits any new slab-on-grade flooring install needs to meet in a Sarasota-area home, whether or not a flood was ever involved.
- [How Long Does Flooring Need to Acclimate in Florida Before Installation?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/long-flooring-acclimate-florida-before-installation/): There's no set number of days. The NWFA judges acclimation by moisture-meter readings, not a calendar, and only starts counting once the HVAC has run at normal living conditions for at least 48 hours. Strip flooring needs to land within 4% moisture content of the subfloor, wide plank within 2%, before installation in a Sarasota-area home.
- [Can I Live in My House During Floor Removal and Installation?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/live-house-during-floor-removal-installation/): Yes, most Sarasota-area homeowners stay in the house during a floor replacement. A two-person crew clears about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days, so we work room by room, sealing off finished areas and containing dust, and most families are back to normal in a zone within a day or two.
- [Is Laminate Flooring a Bad Idea in Florida Homes?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/laminate-flooring-bad-idea-florida/): Not automatically, but it needs the right product and prep: Sarasota's outdoor humidity averages 74% year-round, and standard laminate swells if moisture reaches its core. Water-resistant laminate with a WetProtect-style warranty covers spills, pet accidents and wet mopping, but excludes flooding and standing water. Over concrete, Mohawk requires a 6-mil polyethylene moisture barrier with 8-inch overlapped seams before any laminate goes down.
- [How Do I Keep Beach Sand From Scratching My Floors?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/keep-beach-sand-scratching-floors/): Shaw's vinyl care guide recommends cleaning weekly, using mats without latex or rubber backing (which can discolor vinyl), and adding felt protectors under furniture to keep grit from grinding into the finish. A 20-mil wear layer also holds up to sand better than the standard 12-mil grade. For Sarasota-area beach traffic, a weekly vacuum or dry mop before wet-cleaning removes grit before it gets ground in.
- [Can New Flooring Go Over Your Existing Tile?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/install-new-flooring-over-existing-tile/): Yes, in most cases. Rigid-core flooring can go over existing tile if the tile is fully adhered, clean, and flat within 3/16 inch over 10 feet. If it fails that flatness test or has loose or cracked tiles, removal typically runs $2.50-$4.50 per square foot, more on a thick mortar bed, before the new floor goes down.
- [Can You Install Hardwood Flooring Directly on a Concrete Slab?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/install-hardwood-flooring-directly-concrete-slab/): Engineered hardwood can glue directly to a concrete slab that tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours (ASTM F1869). Solid hardwood traditionally needs a built-up plywood subfloor over the slab first, since the NWFA advises against installing solid wood below grade or directly on bare concrete in a Sarasota-area home.
- [What Indoor Humidity Should I Keep for Wood Floors in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/indoor-humidity-keep-wood-floors-florida/): Keep indoor relative humidity between 30% and 50%, per NWFA guidelines, with temperature around 60-80°F, to protect hardwood and engineered floors in Sarasota and Manatee County homes. Outdoor air here averages about 74% RH year-round, climbing to roughly 78% in August, so a well-sized AC system running consistently does most of the work.
- [What IIC Rating Does Florida Condo Flooring Need?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/iic-rating-condo-flooring-florida/): Florida's building code requires a minimum IIC and STC of 50 between condo floors (45 if field-tested), but that's just the legal floor. Most Sarasota-area associations want 55 to 60, and luxury towers often push higher. The real number lives in your condo declaration and rules, not the state code, so read those documents before you buy flooring or underlayment.
- [Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Flood-Damaged Floors in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/homeowners-insurance-cover-flood-damaged-floors-florida/): No, not under a standard homeowners policy. FEMA is explicit that flood damage, including flooring destroyed by storm surge, requires separate flood insurance. NFIP building coverage goes up to $250,000 and contents coverage up to $100,000, but new policies usually carry a 30-day waiting period, so buying flood coverage after a storm's already forecast for Sarasota County is typically too late.
- [How Do You Get HOA Approval for New Flooring in a Sarasota Condo?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/hoa-approval-new-flooring-sarasota-condo/): Most Sarasota-area condo boards want a renovation application with flooring and underlayment spec sheets, an acoustic test report, and installer insurance certificates before they approve a job. Siesta Dunes, for example, requires an underlayment rated at least IIC 50 under every hard floor above the first floor and prohibits floating floors entirely in those units.
- [What Does Installed Hardwood Flooring Cost Per Square Foot?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/hardwood-flooring-cost-per-square-foot-installed/): Installed hardwood flooring typically costs $9 to $24 per square foot in 2026, in Sarasota and Manatee County. Standard 5 in. engineered runs $9-$12, solid 3/4 in. nail-down runs $10-$14, and wide-plank European white oak or herringbone patterns run $14-$24. Board width, wood species, pattern complexity and whether the job is a slab or plywood subfloor all move the price.
- [Is Glue-Down or Floating Better for Floors on a Florida Concrete Slab?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/glue-down-floating-better-floors-florida-concrete-slab/): Neither is universally better; it depends on the room and the building. Glue-down handles higher slab moisture and heavy traffic better because the adhesive itself can be rated for the reading, while floating installs faster and is easier to replace in sections. Some Sarasota-area condo buildings, including Siesta Key's Siesta Dunes, prohibit floating floors above the first floor entirely.
- [What Flooring Survives a Hurricane Flood in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-survives-hurricane-flood-florida/): No flooring type is truly hurricane-proof, but materials with very low water absorption hold up best. FEMA's Technical Bulletin 2 sorts building materials into Classes 1 through 5 by flood damage resistance, requiring Class 4 or 5 below the base flood elevation in a Special Flood Hazard Area. Porcelain tile, defined by ANSI as absorbing 0.5% or less water, is a common choice in Sarasota-area homes near open water.
- [Why Are Flooring Quotes in Sarasota So Different From Each Other?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-quotes-sarasota-different-each-other/): Two Sarasota flooring quotes for the same room can differ by thousands of dollars because they scope different work under one number. One contractor's price might include demo, slab leveling and moisture testing; another's might cover material and labor only, with everything else billed later. The gap is almost always in what's included, not in the flooring product itself.
- [Does Florida Require a License to Install Flooring?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-installers-license-florida/): No. Florida issues no state license for flooring or tile installers, and as of July 1, 2024, cities and counties can no longer require one either, under a preemption law passed as HB 735 in 2021 and expanded by HB 1383 in 2023. Installers still need an active Sunbiz business registration and general liability insurance, plus workers' compensation or a valid exemption.
- [What Flooring Holds Up Best to Dog Urine?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-holds-up-dog-urine/): Tile and waterproof LVP hold up best to dog urine, since neither has an absorbent core at the surface: urine is acidic and only causes lasting stain or odor damage once it seeps into a seam and reaches a wood core or subfloor. A 20-mil wear layer adds extra seam protection for high-traffic Sarasota-area households. Water-resistant laminate's Pergo WetProtect warranty covers pet accidents too, but excludes standing water.
- [What Flooring Are Florida Buyers Actually Looking For?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-florida-home-buyers-want/): Florida home buyers generally expect tile, luxury vinyl plank or engineered hardwood underfoot, according to Floor Coverings International's Florida resale guidance. Worn carpet and dated tile, yellowed grout, small dark tiles from an earlier decade, are the two objections that come up most often during showings. Matching your flooring to what buyers already expect reduces hesitation during a walkthrough.
- [What's the Best Flooring for a Snowbird Home Sitting Empty All Summer?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flooring-best-snowbird-home-sits-empty-all-summer/): Rigid-core SPC vinyl plank is the safest pick for a Florida snowbird home, since some SPC lines are rated to handle temperatures from -25 F to 155 F once installed. Keep the AC running at no higher than 85 F while you're away; UF/IFAS warns that above that, indoor humidity passes 55-60% and mold can start growing.
- [Why Is a Tile Popping Up or Sounding Hollow When You Walk On It?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/floor-tiles-popping-up-sounding-hollow/): Hollow or popping tile is almost always caused by missing movement joints combined with a weak mortar bond, not one single defect. TCNA's EJ171 standard calls for movement joints every 20-25 feet indoors, but every 8-12 feet where tile sits in direct sun or gets wet - common on Florida lanais and pool baths.
- [Which Tile Stays Safe to Walk On When It's Wet?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/floor-tile-not-slippery-wet/): Look for a tile rated at a wet DCOF of 0.42 or higher, the ANSI A137.1/A326.3 minimum for interior floors expected to get walked on wet, including Florida bathrooms and kitchens. That number comes from a lab test, not a guarantee for every spill; texture, grout joint width and how you clean the floor also affect how it feels underfoot.
- [How Flat Does Your Subfloor Need to Be for Large-Format Tile?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flat-floor-large-format-tile/): Large-format tile, meaning any edge 15 inches or longer, needs a substrate flat within 1/8 inch over 10 feet and 1/16 inch over 24 inches, per ANSI A108.02. Most Sarasota and Manatee County slabs need self-leveling underlayment to meet that standard, which typically runs $3-$9 per sq ft installed in 2026.
- [How Flat Does a Concrete Floor Need to Be for Vinyl Plank Flooring?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/flat-concrete-floor-vinyl-plank-flooring/): Shaw's SPC vinyl plank installation guide requires the slab to be flat within 3/16 in. over a 10 ft span, or 1/8 in. over 6 ft, before install. A slab outside that tolerance needs self-leveling underlayment, which typically runs $250 to $700 per room for us on a Sarasota-area job, depending on how uneven the concrete is.
- [How Fast Can You Replace Floors Between Guest Bookings?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/fast-floors-replaced-between-guest-bookings/): A two-person crew installs about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days on a flat, prepped slab, which fits inside most short-term rental gaps. Tile needs 24 hours before grouting and up to 72 hours before heavy furniture returns, so it rarely fits a same-week turnaround without blocking extra booking days.
- [Is Dustless Tile Removal Worth Paying More For?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/dustless-tile-removal-worth-extra-cost/): Standard ceramic or porcelain tile removal in Southwest Florida runs $2.50-$4.50 per square foot, or $4.00-$6.50-plus on a thick mortar bed, with thinset grinding adding $0.75-$1.25 per square foot. Dustless methods add a premium on top of that baseline; ask for both prices in writing and weigh it against who's living in the house during the work.
- [How Much Should You Pay Upfront for a Flooring Job?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/deposit-pay-flooring-contractor/): A typical flooring contractor deposit runs 10% to 25% of the total job, sometimes up to 50% on smaller jobs where material has to be special-ordered. The rest should be tied to milestones like material delivery, demo completion and finished install, never paid in full before work has started, according to Angi's contractor payment guidance.
- [Do Cupped Hardwood Floors Have to Be Replaced?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/cupped-hardwood-floors-fixed-without-replacing-them/): In humid Sarasota-area homes, mild cupped hardwood often flattens on its own within weeks to months once the moisture source is fixed, without any sanding. NWFA and Wagner Meters both warn against sanding a cupped floor early - sanding before moisture readings return to normal causes the boards to crown instead, a different and worse problem.
- [How Much Does It Cost to Remove Old Tile Flooring?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/cost-remove-tile-flooring-southwest-florida/): Removing ceramic or porcelain tile flooring in Southwest Florida costs $2.50 to $4.50 per square foot in 2026, rising to $4.00-$6.50 or more when the tile sits on a thick mortar bed instead of thinset. Saltillo runs $3.50-$6.00 per square foot to remove and terrazzo runs $3.00-$5.50, both common in older Sarasota and Manatee County homes.
- [What Does Refinishing Hardwood Floors Cost?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/cost-refinish-hardwood-floors/): Refinishing hardwood floors runs $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026, close to HomeGuide's national range of $2-$8 per sq ft. A typical whole-home job costs $800-$3,200. Dustless refinishing, recommended for occupied homes, runs $5-$8 per sq ft nationally per Angi.
- [How Much Does Vinyl Plank Flooring Cost to Install in Sarasota?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/cost-install-vinyl-plank-flooring-sarasota-fl/): Installed vinyl plank flooring in Sarasota and Manatee County typically runs $1.75 to $9.50 per square foot in 2026. Standard 12-mil product installs for $1.75-$3.25, mid-range 20-mil SPC for $2.75-$5.50, and wide-plank luxury vinyl for $5.50-$9.50. The spread depends on wear layer thickness, core material, and whether old flooring has to come out first.
- [What Do Hardwood Stair Treads Cost Installed?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/cost-install-hardwood-stair-treads/): Hardwood stair treads typically run $130-$220 per tread installed in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026, with risers adding $25-$65 each. A 13-step staircase runs roughly $1,700-$2,900 for treads alone. National averages from HomeGuide and Angi land close, around $100-$250 per step installed.
- [Should You Refinish Your Hardwood Floors or Replace Them?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/better-refinish-replace-hardwood-floors/): For Sarasota and Manatee County homeowners, refinishing existing hardwood typically costs $2-$8 per sq ft, versus $9-$25 per sq ft installed for new hardwood - refinishing wins on cost when the floor is structurally sound. The NAR/NARI 2022 Remodeling Impact Report found hardwood refinishing recovered 147% of its cost at resale, versus 118% for new wood flooring.
- [Big-Box Flooring or a Local Installer: Which Makes More Sense?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/better-buy-flooring-home-depot-lowes-hire-local/): Both routes can produce a good floor. The real difference is who's accountable on installation day: a big-box store typically dispatches whichever subcontractor is available in your area that week, while a local installer sends the same crew, often the owner, who quoted the job and stands behind the warranty directly if something goes wrong.
- [When's the Best Time of Year to Install Flooring in Sarasota?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-time-year-flooring-installation-sarasota/): Sarasota's outdoor humidity runs about 74% year-round, from roughly 69% in April to 78% in August, so no single month is humidity-free. What matters more is running the HVAC at normal living conditions for at least 48 hours before installers arrive; acclimation is judged by moisture-meter readings, not the calendar date.
- [What's the Best Soundproof Underlayment for a Condo Floor?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-soundproof-underlayment-condo-floors/): Cork, rubber, and dense recycled-foam underlayments are the standard choices for Florida condo floors, with cork alone often reaching IIC 55-60. Florida's building code sets a 50 IIC/STC minimum between units, but many Sarasota-area associations want 55-60 or higher, so get the product's ASTM E2179 test report before you buy anything.
- [What's the Best Flooring for a Florida Vacation Rental?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-flooring-vacation-rental-florida/): Waterproof rigid-core LVP with at least a 20-mil wear layer, or porcelain tile, are the standard picks for Florida vacation rentals. Both shed sand and moisture and outlast the standard 12-mil residential wear layer under guest turnover. Skip carpet, which traps sand and moisture, and solid hardwood, which is harder to protect between bookings.
- [What's the Best Flooring for a Florida Home?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-flooring-florida-home/): In Sarasota and Manatee County homes built on a concrete slab, waterproof rigid-core LVP and porcelain tile handle Florida's humid climate best, since outdoor humidity averages 74% year-round. Engineered hardwood works too if the slab tests within the manufacturer's moisture limit. Solid hardwood only makes sense in a climate-controlled room, never over a slab that reads wet.
- [What's the Best Flooring for an Upper-Floor Condo in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-flooring-florida-condo-upper-floor/): For an upper-floor Florida condo, the safest picks are cork, which can hit IIC 55-60 on its own, tile or wood over a rated acoustic underlayment, or rigid-core vinyl plank with a documented ASTM E2179 test report for the full assembly. Confirm your building's real minimum first; some Sarasota-area associations require IIC/STC 60 or higher.
- [What's the Best Flooring for Dogs?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/best-flooring-dogs/): Waterproof LVP and porcelain or ceramic tile rank highest for scratch, stain and urine resistance, per Angi and HomeGuide reviews. Urine is acidic and can permanently stain a wood core if it reaches it; tile and waterproof LVP don't absorb it the same way. Our verdict for Sarasota-area dog owners: choose 20-mil-plus LVP or tile for large or unhousebroken dogs, standard 12-mil for calmer, smaller ones.
- [Am I Stupid to Want Engineered Wood in Florida?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/am-stupid-want-engineered-wood-florida/): No -- engineered hardwood is the standard choice for Sarasota and Manatee County slabs, not a compromise. Its cross-layered core resists the cupping solid wood can show in humid swings, and it's made to glue directly to concrete. The real trade-off is wear-layer thickness: a 3 mm veneer typically allows only two to three refinishing sandings over its life.
- [Should You Get a 12 Mil or 20 Mil Wear Layer on Vinyl Plank?](https://sarasotaflooringcompany.com/blog/12-mil-20-mil-wear-layer-vinyl-plank/): A 12-mil wear layer (0.012 inch) is the standard residential option and fine for light-traffic rooms. A 20-mil wear layer (0.020 inch) is the usual commercial minimum and the better call for large dogs, kids, or a rental property that turns over often. Our verdict: pay the difference for 20-mil in high-traffic Sarasota-area homes and rentals.
